title: The Animal With Three Hearts
paragraphs: An octopus is a soft sea animal with eight arms. It has no bones, so it can squeeze through very small holes. But the most surprising things about it are inside its body. Scientists often study it to learn how clever animals can be.

First, an octopus has three hearts. Two hearts push blood through the gills, and the third sends it around the rest of the body. Its blood is blue, because it carries oxygen with a substance that contains copper. Our blood is red, because it uses iron. Without these special hearts, an octopus could not live for long.
An octopus also has a clever nervous system. About two thirds of its nerve cells are in its arms, not in its head. Because of this, each arm can do some work by itself.
